original_hook: $MTL is down 21.58% intraday, but the order book volume tells a very different story than the percentage drop suggests. When MTL broke down toward $0.307, 1H sell volume peaked at 582,611 units. Fast forward to the recent consolidation between $0.296 and $0.306: volume collapsed to just 82,614 and 122,549 units. When price stays pinned at lows while aggressive sell volume contracts by nearly 80%, it indicates that taker sell inventory has cleared out into passive bids at $0.296, forcing volatility into a tight coil. The catch. Low volume at support can also mean a total absence of buyer demand—leaving price fragile if fresh market sells hit the book. 📊 MTL 1H: price $0.298 • support $0.296 • resistance $0.384 • TP1 $0.274 • target $0.252 • SL / invalidation $0.384 (short bias). Levels are chart-derived scenarios, not guarantees. What confirmation on $MTL would make you treat this setup as real rather than an early headline move?
